$comment: One lifecycle vocabulary for every capability and pack item, issue #1228 (owner decision, 2026-09-22): before this contract, the loop lifecycle (#1195) and pack item statuses (#1204) were two state models designed side by side, using different words for the same underlying position. This contract is the single source both specialize from. @clossys/controller exports it (packages/controller/src/loop/lifecycle.ts) so Controller's own loop engine, Publisher's pack rendering, and this repository's package-framework manifest checks all import one definition instead of re-declaring their own.

stateMeaning.absent: Nothing exists yet for this capability or item.
stateMeaning.found: It exists but is not yet managed by the loop -- adopt it, never overwrite it.
stateMeaning.draft: Produced by the role, not yet judged.
stateMeaning.approved: Judged and accepted by the accountable party (a role's own judge stage, or the Customer keep for a pack item).
stateMeaning.verified: Independently verified -- for a pack item, sealed and live.
stateMeaning.retired: Deliberately withdrawn; superseded or no longer applicable.

conditionMeaning.current: The state's own evidence still matches its declared inputs.
conditionMeaning.stale: An input, the role itself, or a review window has moved past what produced this state; the loop re-enters per its own trigger table.
conditionMeaning.blocked: The loop cannot advance this capability without an external resolution (see docs/contracts/loop.json's blocker kinds).

packStatusMapping.$comment: Pack item statuses (#1204) specialize this same vocabulary; they are not a second set of words. Every pack status maps onto exactly one lifecycle state, and the three renamed ones also carry the extra meaning the mapping states.

governance.rule: No package other than @clossys/controller declares its own copy of `states` or `conditions`. A surface that needs a specialized vocabulary (like pack statuses) maps onto these six states and three conditions rather than inventing new words, and records that mapping next to its own status type.
governance.changeProcedure: A change to `states` or `conditions` is exactly one pull request: it bumps this file's own `schemaVersion`, updates packages/controller/src/loop/lifecycle.ts in the same change, and brings every consumer's own mapping into conformance.
